tier_reason: README Performance section shows benchmark-ips results vs Ruby stdlib CSV (163.4 vs 1,013.7 i/s = 6.20x; 5.27x; 5.00x; 4.33x) and the script is public (benchmark/parse_bench.rb), but only the Ruby version (3.4.7) is stated -- no CPU model, compiler or flags, so first-party Tier C.

corrections.caveats: No CPU model or compiler flags stated for the benchmark (only Ruby 3.4.7), so it cannot exceed Tier C, although the benchmark script is public (benchmark/parse_bench.rb, benchmark-ips; memory in benchmark/memory_bench.rb). Synthetic data only (value_i_j fields, no quoting). Extremely small/new project (17 stars, single author, README says it was built with Claude Code), so treat numbers as unverified by outside parties; the underlying speedup is really zsv's (liquidaty/zsv 1.4.3), wrapped for Ruby.

notes: All numbers match the README verbatim (string allocations are 56.9% fewer). Metadata checked: MIT, not a fork, 17 stars, last commit 2026-07-30. It is a Ruby binding of liquidaty/zsv (also a wave-3 known-list entry); the orchestrator may prefer to fold it under zsv rather than list it separately.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed ASPLOS '26 paper (DOI 10.1145/3779212.3790227) that picks flex as its main baseline and says 'StreamTok is 2-3 times faster than flex' (RQ3, Fig. 10), with CPUs stated (Xeon E5-2640 v4 for RQ1-2; EPYC 7252 for RQ3-6). No public code, Rust compiler or flags found, so it cannot be A.

corrections.caveats: Peer-reviewed ASPLOS '26 paper (Li, Yang, Mamouras, Rice University; DOI 10.1145/3779212.3790227) with a detailed experimental section, but no public StreamTok source/artifact repository was found (the paper text links none), and the paper does not state the Rust compiler version or build flags, so it stays at Tier B. benchmark_url is a third-party mirror of the paper text (bojieli/ai-infra-book); the canonical DOI page on dl.acm.org blocks automated fetches. At the application level (RQ5, Table 2) the paper reports 2.5x-3.1x for log-to-TSV and up to 5.39x (JSON minify) over flex.

notes: Claims, hardware and workload list (csv, dns, fasta, json, log, tsv, XML, yaml; the 10 MB (a{0,k}b)|a microbenchmark) all match the paper text. baseline_in_list set to false because this category's baseline list is 're2c, hand-written baselines the benchmark names', which does not include flex. I found no code under the kmamouras GitHub account; I did not search further because gh search and WebSearch were not allowed.

tier_reason: The FAQ states 'over 10 times faster than Flex/Bison parser tools' and 'approximately 10 times faster than Flex/Bison tools' with no methodology. The repo's bench/ directory only covers SQLite/STL map/Boost multi-index, with no parser-vs-Flex/Bison benchmark, so this is a first-party number without methodology: Tier C.
notes: Quotes, MPL-2.0, 268 stars, last commit 2025-06-20 (stale) all verified. A hand-written parser exists in src/parser/xdb_parser*.c. baseline_in_list set to false because Flex/Bison is not in this category's baseline list ('re2c, hand-written baselines the benchmark names').

tier_reason: The DFA page says 'These are TWO TIMES the speed of "flex" created lexers' and that re2c lexers are 'up to 10% faster than DFA lexers'. It gives no corpus, code, compiler, flags or hardware, so this is a first-party number without methodology: Tier C.

corrections.caveats: First-party claim with a number but no stated compiler, flags, hardware, benchmark corpus, or linked benchmark code -- capped at Tier C. The upstream SourceForge page states a different figure ('a DFA lexer generator, 80% faster than flex lexers'), so the size of the gain is inconsistent. By the same author's account, re2c lexers are up to 10% faster, so LRSTAR does not beat re2c. p7r0x7/LRSTAR is a third-party 'maintenance fork' (per its GitHub description; not a GitHub fork) of Paul B Mann's SourceForge project (last updated there 2024-07-09); its recent commits are GitHub linguist tweaks. Code is BSD-3-Clause (doc/software_license.txt, source_dfa/license.txt); GitHub reports no license because there is no root LICENSE file. The website HTML pages are '(c) Paul B Mann 2023, All rights reserved'.

notes: benchmark_url used branch 'main', which returns 404; the repo's only branch is 'master'. License fixed from null to BSD-3-Clause after reading the two license files, so usability changes to copyable. 0 stars and last commit 2026-04-19 verified; the canonical project is arguably sourceforge.net/projects/lrstar rather than this mirror.

tier_reason: The Ragel 3.7 ChangeLog entry (Oct 31, 2004) only says the Ragel version of examples/cppscan 'goes faster than flex version but not as fast as re2c version'. There are no numbers, so Tier D. It is kept despite <1k stars because Ragel is widely used (e.g. HarfBuzz src/*.rl, Puma's ext/puma_http11/http11_parser.rl).

corrections.workload: C++ tokenizer example (examples/cppscan) written three ways -- Ragel (cppscan.rl), flex (cppscan.lex) and re2c (cppscan.rec) -- and compared informally, per the Ragel 3.7 ChangeLog entry (Oct 31, 2004)
corrections.stars_or_usage: 239 stars on adrian-thurston/colm-suite (current home); 619 stars on the archived adrian-thurston/ragel repo; Ragel-generated state machines are used in HarfBuzz (8 .rl sources in src/) and Puma's HTTP parser (ext/puma_http11/http11_parser.rl)
corrections.caveats: Only a directional claim with no numbers, methodology, compiler flags, or hardware -- a Tier D entry (capped at one per run), included because Ragel is a long-standing, widely used project, not because the flex claim is strong. The claim dates from Ragel 3.7 (2004), so it is about 22 years old and refers to an early code generator. Ragel is not claimed to beat re2c. The original adrian-thurston/ragel GitHub repo is archived; active development continues under adrian-thurston/colm-suite, used as the canonical URL here.

notes: Quote verified verbatim in src/ragel/ChangeLog under 'Ragel 3.7 - Oct 31, 2004'. The comparison is in examples/, not the test suite. The benchmark_url branch 'master' 302-redirects to 'main'. MIT, not archived, last commit 2026-09-25, ragel repo archived with 619 stars: all verified. I could not verify the Gherkin usage claim, so I replaced it with the HarfBuzz and Puma usage I did verify. baseline_in_list set to false because flex is not in this category's baseline list.
